questions.question: Which of the following characteristics is **not **associated with inflation?

options.text: The value of money is rising
Excess of demand over available supply

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **the value of money is rising.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Inflation **is the **continuous rise in the price of a commodity**. It **reduces the purchasing power **of the consumers and **makes goods costlier.**
 
• Inflation helps to **increase exports** because **goods become cheaper** in the **foreign market** and **reduces imports** because** goods become costlier** in the **domestic market.**
 
• Inflation **increases the amount of money **but **reduces its value**. It means that more amount of money has to be spent to get the same unit of quantity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Types of inflation involve-__

 
 
• **Demand-pull**- When aggregate demand exceeds aggregate supply in the economy. 
 
• **Cost-push**- When price rises, due to a rise in any of the factors of production (land, labour, capital and entrepreneur).
 
 

**Hence, the correct answer is*** that the value of money rising is not associated with inflation.*

questions.question: The "Ministry of Jal Shakti" was formed by merging "Ministry of Water Resources, River Development & Ganga Rejuvenation" along with?

options.text: Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation
The Ministry of Environment and Forests

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ministry of Jal Shakti was formed in May 2019 by merging the **Ministry of Water Resources, River Development & Ganga Rejuvenation** and the **Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation**.
 
• This move aimed at integrating management of water resources and supply across India under a single umbrella ministry.
 
• The Ministry of Jal Shakti focuses on issues related to water conservation, supply, management, and sanitation, including the implementation of flagship programs like the **Jal Jeevan Mission**.
 
• The merger was part of the government’s efforts to streamline policies and strengthen the institutional framework for addressing water-related challenges in the country.
 
• The Ministry also oversees the **National Water Mission** and other initiatives aimed at ensuring sustainable water use and equitable distribution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jal Jeevan Mission:**

 
 
• Launched in 2019, this mission aims to provide **functional household tap connections (FHTC)** to every rural household by 2024.
 
• It emphasizes the importance of community participation in water resource management.
 
• The program also focuses on water quality monitoring and capacity building at the village level.
 
 
 
• **National Water Mission:**
 
 
• This mission is part of India’s National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC).
 
• Its objective is to **conserve water, minimize waste, and ensure equitable distribution** across regions.
 
• The mission promotes the development of basin-level water resource management strategies.
 
 
 
• **Swachh Bharat Mission:**
 
 
• Previously implemented under the Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation, now part of Jal Shakti Ministry.
 
• It aims to eliminate open defecation and improve sanitation facilities across India.
 
• The program has significantly contributed to improving hygiene and water-related health outcomes.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Water Resource Management (IWRM):**
 
 
• This concept promotes coordinated development and management of water resources to maximize economic and social welfare.
 
• The Ministry of Jal Shakti plays a key role in implementing IWRM strategies nationwide.

questions.question: The 'Arabian Sea Branch' and the 'Bay of Bengal Branch' are associated with which weather system in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**South-West Monsoon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arabian Sea Branch and Bay of Bengal Branch:** These are the two distinct streams of the **South-West Monsoon** that originate and move across different regions of India.
 
• The **Arabian Sea Branch** originates over the Arabian Sea and brings heavy rainfall to the western coast of India, including areas like **Kerala, Karnataka, Goa, and Maharashtra**. It is influenced by the Western Ghats, which enhance precipitation due to orographic lifting.
 
• The **Bay of Bengal Branch** originates over the Bay of Bengal and moves towards the northeastern states like **Assam, Meghalaya, and West Bengal**. It also travels further north towards the Indo-Gangetic plains, bringing rainfall to regions like **Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and Punjab**.
 
• The **South-West Monsoon** is the primary monsoon system in India, responsible for approximately **75%-80%** of the annual rainfall. It is critical for agriculture, water resources, and overall economic activities in the country. *Hence, the correct answer is South-West Monsoon.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **South-West Monsoon System:**

 
 
• It is characterized by the reversal of wind patterns due to the differential heating of land and water bodies. The monsoon winds blow from the south-west direction towards the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The system is influenced by factors like the **Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)**, the **El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO)**, and the presence of high-pressure systems in the southern hemisphere.
 
 
 
• **Arabian Sea Branch:**
 
 
• This branch covers the western coast of India and brings heavy rainfall due to the **Western Ghats**. The orographic lifting of moist air causes intense precipitation in the region.
 
• Examples of regions receiving rainfall from the Arabian Sea Branch include **Kerala, Mumbai, and Mangalore**.
 
 
 
• **Bay of Bengal Branch:**
 
 
• This branch moves towards the northeastern states and then spreads across the Indo-Gangetic plains. Rainfall is enhanced in regions with plains and foothills.
 
• **Example:** States like **Assam** and **Bihar** receive rainfall due to this branch.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Importance:**
 
 
• The South-West Monsoon is crucial for crops like **rice, sugarcane, pulses, and cotton**. Farmers depend heavily on monsoon rainfall for irrigation.
 
• Regions like the Indo-Gangetic plains are highly dependent on monsoon rainfall for their **agricultural economy**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Weather Systems in India:**

 
 
• **Pre-Monsoon:** This period is characterized by localized thunderstorms, heat waves, and cyclonic activities, especially in April and May.
 
• **Tornadoes:** Rare in India but can occur in regions like West Bengal and Odisha during extreme weather conditions.
 
• **North-East Monsoon:** Occurs primarily in southern states like **Tamil Nadu** and brings rainfall during October to December.
 
 
 
• **Global Factors:**
 
 
• The **El Niño** and **La Niña** phenomena significantly influence monsoon behavior, leading to droughts or excessive rainfall.
 
• The monsoon system is also affected by **global warming** and climate change, which can alter rainfall patterns.

 __

• The mutineers took out a procession in Bombay, holding aloft a portrait of Subhas Bose.

• The strike **started in Bombay harbour** where a contingent of ratings had arrived. The ratings of HMIS Talwar, a shore establishment also had seething discontent against their seniors for similar reasons.
 
• On 19 February a **Naval Central Strike committee was formed with Leading Signalman Lieutenant M.S. Khan and Petty Officer Telegraphist Madan Singh** elected as president and vice-president respectively.
 
• The strikers were inspired by the INA trials and the persona of Subhas Chandra Bose.
 
 
• Soon, the strike evolved into open revolt with many cities joining the Bombay sailors.
 
• **Sailors from Karachi, Calcutta, Poona, Vizag, and Cochin joined involving 66 ships and shore establishments.**
 
 
 
• Ratings were not obeying their officers and they conducted demonstrations in the city of Bombay leaving their posts.
 
• The city of Bombay particularly was tense.
 
 
• Hundreds of protestors targeted the British residents and officers of the city.
 
• **They even took control of Butcher Island where the entire ammunition of the Bombay Presidency was stored.**
 
 
 
• **The rebels also found support from the Royal Indian Air Force men from Bombay and from the Gurkhas in Karachi who, known for their loyalty, refused to fire at the strikers.**
 
• The open revolt struck at the heart of the British establishment who now realized that the armed forces, which was one of their key tools in maintaining their mastery over the subcontinent, could no longer be relied upon.
 
• The sailors displayed a strong unity cutting across lines of religion and region despite the impending partition of the country on communal lines.
 
• The revolt, however, failed to see support from the Indian leadership who perhaps saw a mutiny, so close to independence, as a danger.
 
 
• Only the Communist Party of India and the INC’s **Aruna Asaf Ali openly supported the sailors.**
 
 
 
• **The mutiny came to an end with the intervention of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. **
 
 
• The mutineers surrendered on 23 February 1946.
 
 
 
• A total of 7 sailors and 1 officer were killed. 476 sailors were discharged as a result of the mutiny. They were not taken into the Indian or Pakistani navies after independence.
 
• It is noteworthy to point out that there was massive public support for the mutineers. During the violence in Bombay that ensued because of the strike, over 200 civilians had died.​** **

questions.question: Among the following crops, which one is the most important anthropogenic source of both methane and nitrous oxide ?

• Irrigated rice or paddy crop cultivation has been identified as one of the leading global agricultural sources of anthropogenic methane (CH4) emissions.
 
• It has been estimated that global rice production is responsible for 11% of total anthropogenic CH4 emissions.
 
• Irrigated rice fields are the major source of methane from rice fields.
 
• Although irrigated rice comprises only 50% of the harvested rice area, it produces 70% of the rice harvested.

• **The greenhouse effect is a natural phenomenon that insulates the Earth from the cold of space.**
 
• As incoming solar radiation is absorbed and re-emitted back from the Earth’s surface as infrared energy, greenhouse gases (GHGs) in the atmosphere prevent some of this heat from escaping into space, instead of reflecting the energy back to further warm the surface.
 
• **Anthropogenic (human-caused) GHG emissions are modifying the Earth’s energy balance between incoming solar radiation and the heat released back into space**, amplifying the greenhouse effect and resulting in climate change.

• The **Output method** measures the total value of goods and services produced in an economy.
 
• The **Income method** sums up all the incomes earned by individuals and businesses, including wages, profits, rents, and interest.
 
• Each of these methods provides a different perspective on the economic activity and can be used to cross-verify the accuracy of the national income calculations.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The tropical wet and dry climate is characterized by **high temperatures throughout the year**, typically above 18°C on average.
 
• Rainfall is highly variable, with a distinct **short wet season** followed by a longer dry season.
 
• This climate type is primarily found in regions located near the tropics, such as **Sudan and Paraguay**.
 
• The tropical wet and dry climate is commonly associated with the **savanna ecosystem**, supporting grasslands interspersed with trees.
 
• It is influenced by the movement of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ), which brings seasonal shifts in rainfall.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ):**

 
 
• ITCZ is a belt of low pressure that encircles the Earth near the equator.
 
• It shifts north and south seasonally, influencing rainfall patterns in tropical regions.
 
 
 
• **Savanna Ecosystem:**
 
 
• Characterized by grasslands with scattered trees, it is common in tropical wet and dry climate regions.
 
• Supports diverse flora and fauna, including herbivores like zebras and carnivores like lions.
 
 
 
• **Climate Classification:**
 
 
• As per the Köppen climate classification, tropical wet and dry climate is denoted as **Aw**.
 
• It contrasts with tropical rainforest climates (Af) due to its distinct dry season.
 
 
 
• **Global Examples:**
 
 
• Besides Sudan and Paraguay, other regions with this climate include parts of Brazil, India, and northern Australia.
 
• These areas often support agriculture and tourism based on their seasonal rainfall patterns.

⇒ 1 year SI = 1322.40 ÷ 3 = ₹440.80

Amount after 4 years (A₄) = ₹7563.20

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

⇒ Principal (P) = A₁ − SI for 1 year

⇒ P = 6240.80 − 440.80 = 5800

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (SI for 1 year × 100) ÷ P

⇒ R = (440.80 × 100) ÷ 5800

⇒ R = 44080 ÷ 5800 = 7.6%

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5800, 7.6%.**

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the principal remains constant every year, meaning the interest generated is the same annually. In Compound Interest, the accumulated interest of past periods is added to the principal to form the base for the next period.

Principal from Amounts Rule

If a principal becomes A₁ in T₁ years and A₂ in T₂ years under Simple Interest, the principal can be directly calculated as P = A₁ − [ (A₂ − A₁) ÷ (T₂ − T₁) ] × T₁.

Constant SI Property

Since Simple Interest does not compound, the interest accrued over any N-year period is always directly proportional to N, making it uniformly additive.

questions.question: Akbar can complete a piece of work alone in 12 days, while Anthony can complete the same work alone in 20 days. If they work on alternate days with Anthony starting the work, then in how many days can they complete the whole work?

Total work = LCM(12, 20) = 60 units.

Efficiency: Akbar = 5 units/day, Anthony = 3 units/day.

In a 2-day cycle (Anthony first, then Akbar), work done = 3 + 5 = 8 units.

In 7 cycles (14 days), work done = 7 × 8 = 56 units. Remaining work = 60 − 56 = 4 units.

Day 15: Anthony does 3 units. Remaining 1 unit is done by Akbar on Day 16 in 1/5 day.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 1/5 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Akbar = 12 days

Time taken by Anthony = 20 days

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total work is the LCM of 12 and 20 = 60 units.

⇒ Work done in the first 2 days = Anthony's efficiency + Akbar's efficiency = 3 + 5 = 8 units.

⇒ Number of complete 2-day cycles to reach near 60 = 60 ÷ 8 = 7 cycles (with 4 units remaining).

⇒ Time taken for 7 complete cycles = 7 × 2 = 14 days.

Alternate Day Work

When workers work on alternate days, find the combined work done in one complete cycle (usually 2 days for two workers). Multiply the cycle to get as close to total work as possible without exceeding it, then calculate the remaining work day-by-day based on who started.

questions.question: The profit earned when an article is sold for Rs. 800 is 20 times the loss incurred when it is sold for Rs. 275. At what price should the article be sold if it is desired to make a profit of 25%.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Profit to Loss = 20 : 1.

Total difference in SP = 800 − 275 = Rs. 525.

Value of 21 parts (Total Gap) = 525 ⇒ 1 part (Loss) = 525 ÷ 21 = Rs. 25.

Cost Price = Lower SP + Loss = 275 + 25 = Rs. 300.

New Selling Price for 25% profit = 300 × (125 ÷ 100) = Rs. 375.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 375.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price 1 (SP₁) = Rs. 275 (sold at a loss)

Selling Price 2 (SP₂) = Rs. 800 (sold at a profit)

Profit obtained = 20 × Loss incurred

**Formula Used:**

Loss = Cost Price (CP) − Selling Price

Profit = Selling Price − Cost Price (CP)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b6e65797bc85e6644f0a7255df63ea17be0a2c53f1f415a085c079176ac1c0e0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Profit at SP₂ = 20 × Loss at SP₁

⇒ 800 − CP = 20 × (CP − 275)

⇒ 800 − CP = 20CP − 5500

⇒ 20CP + CP = 800 + 5500

⇒ 21CP = 6300

⇒ CP = 6300 ÷ 21 = Rs. 300

⇒ To make a 25% profit, the new selling price must be 125% of the Cost Price.

⇒ New Selling Price = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

⇒ New Selling Price = 300 × (125 ÷ 100)

⇒ New Selling Price = 300 × 1.25 = Rs. 375

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 375.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) of an article. The fundamental formula is: Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount percentage is calculated as: a + b − (a × b ÷ 100).

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer claims to sell goods at cost price but uses a false weight, the actual Profit % = [Error ÷ (True Weight − Error)] × 100.
</p

questions.question: If x is subtracted from each of 52, 47, 20 and 19, the number so obtained in this order are in proportion. What is the mean proportional between (x + 13) and (x - 8)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For numbers a, b, c, d to be in proportion when x is subtracted: x = (ad − bc) ÷ ((a + d) − (b + c))

Here, a = 52, b = 47, c = 20, d = 19

x = (52 × 19 − 47 × 20) ÷ ((52 + 19) − (47 + 20)) = (988 − 940) ÷ (71 − 67) = 48 ÷ 4 = 12

Mean proportional between (x + 13) and (x − 8) = √((12 + 13) × (12 − 8)) = √(25 × 4) = √100 = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers: 52, 47, 20, 19

When x is subtracted from each, they become proportional.

**Formula Used:**

If a, b, c, and d are in proportion, then a ÷ b = c ÷ d.

Mean proportional between two numbers p and q = √(p × q)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b4d3826141a9fdd439c4410d6fbe8fa43baf6014e65dc5053757c47b7ae57d90.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (52 − x) : (47 − x) :: (20 − x) : (19 − x)

⇒ (52 − x) ÷ (47 − x) = (20 − x) ÷ (19 − x)

⇒ (52 − x)(19 − x) = (20 − x)(47 − x)

⇒ 988 − 52x − 19x + x² = 940 − 20x − 47x + x²

⇒ 988 − 71x = 940 − 67x

⇒ 71x − 67x = 988 − 940

⇒ 4x = 48

⇒ x = 12

Now, finding the given terms to calculate the mean proportional:

⇒ First term = (x + 13) = 12 + 13 = 25

⇒ Second term = (x − 8) = 12 − 8 = 4

⇒ Mean proportional = √(25 × 4) = √100 = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is given by √(a × b). It represents the value x such that a : x :: x : b.

Third Proportional

If a, b, and c are in continued proportion (a : b :: b : c), then c is the third proportional to a and b. Formula: c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

For numbers a, b, and c, the fourth proportional is x such that a : b :: c : x. Formula: x = (b × c) ÷ a.

Componendo and Dividendo

If a ÷ b = c ÷ d, then applying Componendo and Dividendo gives (a + b) ÷ (a − b) = (c + d) ÷ (c − d). This rule is widely used to simplify complex ratios.
</p

questions.question: Find the value of (cot(α)/(2) tanα - 1) (2 - tanα.sin2α) =?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Put α = 60°.

First bracket: cot(60°/2) × tan60° − 1 = cot30° × tan60° − 1 = √3 × √3 − 1 = 2.

Second bracket: 2 − tan60° × sin120° = 2 − √3 × (√3/2) = 2 − 3/2 = 1/2.

Result = 2 × 1/2 = 1.

Checking options for α = 60°, only Option 3 yields 2cos60° = 2 × 1/2 = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 2cosα.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(cot(α/2) tanα − 1) (2 − tanα sin2α)

**Calculations:**

Simplify the first bracket:

⇒ cot(α/2) = cos(α/2) / sin(α/2)

⇒ tanα = sinα / cosα = [2sin(α/2) cos(α/2)] / cosα

⇒ cot(α/2) tanα = [cos(α/2) / sin(α/2)] × [2sin(α/2) cos(α/2) / cosα]

⇒ cot(α/2) tanα = 2cos²(α/2) / cosα

⇒ Using half-angle formula, 2cos²(α/2) = 1 + cosα

⇒ First bracket = (1 + cosα) / cosα − 1 = (1 / cosα) + 1 − 1 = 1 / cosα

Simplify the second bracket:

⇒ 2 − tanα sin2α

⇒ 2 − (sinα / cosα) × (2sinα cosα)

⇒ 2 − 2sin²α

⇒ 2(1 − sin²α) = 2cos²α

Multiply both simplified parts:

⇒ Result = (1 / cosα) × 2cos²α

⇒ Result = 2cosα

questions.question: Find the sum of all two digit numbers that give a remainder 3 when they are divided by 8.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The smallest 2-digit number leaving a remainder 3 when divided by 8 is 11, and the largest is 99.

These numbers form an Arithmetic Progression (AP) with a common difference of 8.

Total number of terms (n) = [(99 − 11) ÷ 8] + 1 = 12

Sum = (n ÷ 2) × (First term + Last term)

Sum = (12 ÷ 2) × (11 + 99) = 6 × 110 = 660

**∴ The correct answer is 660.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are two-digit numbers that leave a remainder 3 when divided by 8.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of an AP = (n ÷ 2) × (a + l)

Where a = first term, l = last term, and n = number of terms.

**Calculations:**

⇒ General form of the given numbers = 8k + 3

⇒ For two-digit numbers, the range is: 10 ≤ 8k + 3 ≤ 99

⇒ Subtracting 3 from all sides: 7 ≤ 8k ≤ 96

⇒ Dividing by 8: 0.875 ≤ k ≤ 12

⇒ The possible integer values for k are 1, 2, 3, ..., 12

⇒ First term (a) at k = 1 is 8 × 1 + 3 = 11

⇒ Last term (l) at k = 12 is 8 × 12 + 3 = 99

⇒ Total number of terms (n) = 12

⇒ Sum of these terms = (12 ÷ 2) × (11 + 99)

⇒ Sum = 6 × 110 = 660

**∴ The correct answer is 660.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Progression (AP)

A sequence of numbers in which the difference of any two successive members is a constant. The general term is given by Tₙ = a + (n − 1)d.

Sum of an AP

The sum of the first n terms can be calculated using Sₙ = (n ÷ 2) × [2a + (n − 1)d] or Sₙ = (n ÷ 2) × (a + l) when the first and last terms are known.

Number of Terms in an AP

If the first term a, the last term l, and the common difference d are known, the number of terms is n = [(l − a) ÷ d] + 1.
</p

questions.question: The ratio of the expenditure of A, B, C are 207 : 195 : 217 respectively and their savings are 10%, 25% and 30% of their income. If the sum of their income is Rs. 4,000, Find the difference between the income of A and C.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Income ratio = Expenditure Ratio ÷ Expenditure %

Income ratio = (207 ÷ 90) : (195 ÷ 75) : (217 ÷ 70) = 2.3 : 2.6 : 3.1 = 23 : 26 : 31

Total Income = 23 + 26 + 31 = 80 units

∴ 80 units = 4000 ⇒ 1 unit = 50

Difference between A and C = (31 − 23) units = 8 × 50 = 400

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expenditure ratio of A : B : C = 207 : 195 : 217

Savings % of A = 10%, B = 25%, C = 30%

Sum of their incomes = Rs. 4000

**Formula Used:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings

Expenditure % = 100% − Savings %

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64e4e1a81628b73584ba3cd28e96670cee7fac263160b7e2adea23fe3ee70037.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Expenditure % of A = 100% − 10% = 90%

⇒ Expenditure % of B = 100% − 25% = 75%

⇒ Expenditure % of C = 100% − 30% = 70%

⇒ Let the incomes of A, B and C be IA, IB, and IC.

⇒ 90% of IA : 75% of IB : 70% of IC = 207 : 195 : 217

⇒ IA = (207 × 100) ÷ 90 = 230

⇒ IB = (195 × 100) ÷ 75 = 260

⇒ IC = (217 × 100) ÷ 70 = 310

⇒ Ratio of Incomes = 230 : 260 : 310 = 23 : 26 : 31

⇒ Total Income units = 23 + 26 + 31 = 80 units

⇒ 80 units = Rs. 4000 ⇒ 1 unit = Rs. 50

⇒ Difference between income of C and A = (31 − 23) units = 8 units

⇒ Required difference = 8 × 50 = Rs. 400

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure & Savings

The foundational relationship governing an individual's personal finance is: Income = Expenditure + Savings. If savings are given as a percentage of total income, the expenditure percentage is directly found by subtracting the savings percentage from 100%.

Ratio Comparison Trick

When the ratios of expenditures and their respective percentages are known, the underlying base values (incomes) can be efficiently found by simply dividing each ratio value by its corresponding percentage value. Ratio of bases = Ratio₁ ÷ P₁ : Ratio₂ ÷ P₂.

Compound Ratio Distribution

When partitioning a total quantity according to a combined ratio, the value of 1 fundamental unit equals the total given quantity divided by the aggregate sum of all parts in the ratio. Target portion = Specific Ratio Unit × Value of 1 Unit.

questions.question: The average weight of some students in the class is 38 kg, when 4 new students are added, the average weight becomes 39.5 kg and the weight of those 4 students becomes 46, 52, 36 and 42 kg. Find the total number of students in the class including 4 new students.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average weight of the 4 new students = (46 + 52 + 36 + 42) ÷ 4 = 176 ÷ 4 = 44 kg.

Deviation of the new students' average from the original average = 44 − 38 = +6 kg per student.

Total extra weight added by the 4 new students = 4 × 6 = 24 kg.

This 24 kg extra weight raises the overall average of the entire class by 1.5 kg (from 38 to 39.5).

Total number of students = Total Extra Weight ÷ Increase in Average = 24 ÷ 1.5 = 16.

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial average weight of the class = 38 kg

Weights of the 4 new students = 46 kg, 52 kg, 36 kg, and 42 kg

New average weight of the class = 39.5 kg

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

 
•

• 
 New Combined Avg: 39.5 kg

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial number of students in the class be n.

⇒ Total initial weight of students = 38 × n = 38n kg

⇒ Total weight of the 4 new students = 46 + 52 + 36 + 42 = 176 kg

⇒ New total weight of all students = (38n + 176) kg

⇒ Total number of students now = n + 4

⇒ New average = (38n + 176) ÷ (n + 4)

⇒ 39.5 = (38n + 176) ÷ (n + 4)

⇒ 39.5 × (n + 4) = 38n + 176

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Averages

The average (or arithmetic mean) of a given data set is calculated by dividing the sum of all values by the total number of values: Average = Sum of observations ÷ Total number of observations.

Combined Average

When two groups with counts n₁ and n₂ and individual averages A₁ and A₂ are combined, their overall average is obtained using: Combined Average = (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Net Deviation Method

A powerful shortcut for calculating changes in averages. The change in the average is strictly equal to the net extra (or deficit) value added, divided entirely across the total number of participants: Increase in Average = Net Deviation ÷ Total Count.
</p

questions.question: The ages of Ram and Mohan are in the ratio of 5 : 7 and the difference between them is 12 years. The ages (in years) of Ram and Mohan are respectively:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Difference in ratio parts = 7 − 5 = 2 parts.

2 parts → 12 years.

1 part → 6 years.

Ram's age = 5 parts = 5 × 6 = 30 years.

Mohan's age = 7 parts = 7 × 6 = 42 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 30, 42 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of the ages of Ram and Mohan = 5 : 7

Difference between their ages = 12 years

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/df13f73e145c10c87af97782ecfbcf463759a00dbffbb063ce6eae298c2d8ee9.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the present ages of Ram and Mohan be 5x and 7x respectively.

⇒ According to the given condition, the difference in their ages is 12 years.

⇒ 7x − 5x = 12

⇒ 2x = 12

⇒ x = 12 ÷ 2 = 6

⇒ Present age of Ram = 5x = 5 × 6 = 30 years

⇒ Present age of Mohan = 7x = 7 × 6 = 42 years

**∴ The correct answer is 30, 42 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The age difference between any two individuals always remains constant regardless of the number of years passed (past or future).

Ratio & Proportion Principle

If two quantities are in the ratio a : b, their exact values can be expressed as ax and bx, where x represents a common multiplier.

Sum & Difference Shortcut

When the ratio of two numbers is a : b, the absolute value of 1 ratio part = Difference ÷ (a − b) or Sum ÷ (a + b).
</p

questions.question: A right circular cone of height 15 cm and base radius 15 cm is carved out of a wooden sphere of radius 15 cm. Volume of the remaining wood (in %) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the cone's radius and height are equal to the sphere's radius (R = r = h = 15 cm):

Volume of Cone = (1/3) × π × R³

Volume of Sphere = (4/3) × π × R³

Percentage of volume removed = [(1/3) ÷ (4/3)] × 100 = 25%

Remaining volume = 100% − 25% = 75%

**∴ The correct answer is 75%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the sphere (R) = 15 cm

Radius of the cone (r) = 15 cm

Height of the cone (h) = 15 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a Sphere = (4/3) × πR³

Volume of a Cone = (1/3) × πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8ee93455646685904699e006ec8aec5868f00c5b41d2a7ff53e0082bbe20ce6a.png] 

⇒ Volume of the sphere = (4/3) × π × (15)³

⇒ Volume of the sphere = (4/3) × π × 3375 = 4500π cm³

⇒ Volume of the carved out cone = (1/3) × π × (15)² × 15

⇒ Volume of the carved out cone = (1/3) × π × 3375 = 1125π cm³

⇒ Volume of the remaining wood = 4500π − 1125π = 3375π cm³

⇒ Percentage of remaining wood = (Remaining Volume ÷ Total Volume) × 100

⇒ Percentage = (3375π ÷ 4500π) × 100

⇒ Percentage = 0.75 × 100 = 75%

**∴ The correct answer is 75%.**

Volume of a Sphere

The formula for the volume of a sphere is V = (4/3)πr³, and its total surface area is 4πr².

Volume of a Cone

The formula for the volume of a right circular cone is V = (1/3)πr²h, and its curved surface area is πrl, where l = √(r² + h²).

Percentage Remaining

When a part of a solid is removed, the remaining percentage is calculated as: [(Total Volume − Removed Volume) ÷ Total Volume] × 100.

questions.question: A shopkeeper allows a 25% discount on the marked price of an article and he suffers a loss of 10%. If the article is sold at the marked price, then find the profit percentage.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct ratio formula: MP / CP = (100 − Loss%) / (100 − Discount%)

⇒ MP / CP = (100 − 10) / (100 − 25) = 90 / 75 = 6 / 5

Let Cost Price (CP) = 5 units and Marked Price (MP) = 6 units.

If the article is sold at the marked price, Selling Price (SP) = 6 units.

⇒ Profit % = [(6 − 5) / 5] × 100 = (1 / 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Discount = 25%

Loss = 10%

**Formula Used:**

SP = MP × (100 − D%) / 100

SP = CP × (100 − L%) / 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d88b37289bf1a92aedbb85e3e4245f00005c4b714ce1c382780461b9b9c96a43.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Marked Price (MP) be 100 units.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) after 25% discount = 100 − 25 = 75 units.

⇒ Since there is a 10% loss, SP = CP × (100 − 10) / 100

⇒ 75 = CP × 0.9

⇒ CP = 75 / 0.9 = 250 / 3 units.

⇒ If the article is sold at the Marked Price, New SP = 100 units.

⇒ Profit = New SP − CP = 100 − 250/3 = (300 − 250) / 3 = 50 / 3 units.

⇒ Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = [(50 / 3) / (250 / 3)] × 100 = (50 / 250) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Relation between CP and MP

The ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price is directly derived from profit/loss and discount percentages: CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 ± Profit or Loss%).

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts of D₁% and D₂% are applied on an article, the single equivalent discount is calculated as: D₁ + D₂ − (D₁ × D₂) / 100.

Dishonest Dealer

If a dealer claims to sell goods at Cost Price but uses a false weight, the actual profit percentage is given by: [(True Weight − False Weight) / False Weight] × 100.
</p

questions.question:
This question consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. Rearrange the sentences and choose the correct option.

S1: For a long time, I could not decide whether I should speak to her or not.

S6: At last I moved my lips and told her that her father had passed away.

P: She was anxious to know about her father.

Q: I knew she would start weeping.

R: She looked towards me with anxious eyes.

S: I could not tell her that her father had died before the doctor arrived.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- 'SQRP.' [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• By reading the above-given options we can understand that the author wants to **tell something **to a **girl**.
 
• Part **S **will come **first**, as it shows **why **the author was **not able to speak **to her.
 
• **Q **will come **next**, as it shows the **possible outcome **of the **author's action**.
 
• **P **will follow **R**, as it shows **why **she was **looking anxiously **at the **author.**
 
• Thus *option 2 *is the correct answer.

The correct sequence is:

S1: For a long time, I could not decide whether I should speak to her or not.

S: I could not tell her that her father had died before the doctor arrived.

Q: I knew she would start weeping.

R: She looked towards me with anxious eyes.

​P: She was anxious to know about her father.

S6: At last I moved my lips and told her that her father had passed away. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

 
• Here are some tips to solve the para jumbles:
 
 
• You need to understand the idea behind the paragraph. If you can understand the idea/theme of the paragraph it is easy to put the sentences in order then.
 
• You should look out for the starting or the concluding sentences in the question. Sometimes they are clearly visible and can help you immensely in identifying the correct sequence.
 
• You need to know the relationships between different sentences to put them in the right sequence. 
 
• You should first fix the relationships of sentences, put them in order and then check the options.
 
• Transition words and contrasting words also help in finding clean relationships between sentences of the sentence rearrangement.
 
• Do not over depend on options, they only confuse you if you keep looking at them, use them as facilitators only, especially to fix your first sentence.
 
• The whole paragraph should have a coherent idea and flow when arranged in the correct order.

__
 
• There are some verbs that take fixed prepositions with them.
 
 
• Example: **Refrain from, aim at, abstain from, etc**

• Thus, the correct answer is **option 3.**

 

**Correct sentence:**__ *The newly launched policy is __**aimed at reducing corruption and plugging**__ the loopholes.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• A **gerund** is a verb that’s acting as a noun. By that, we mean that the verb—the word that describes the action that’s happening, like “**biking**,” “**thinking**,” “**running**,” or “**speaking**”—becomes a thing, a concept that can now be the sentence’s subject, direct object, indirect object, or the object of a preposition. 
 
• It doesn’t stop being a verb, but the role it plays in a sentence shifts from describing the action to being a focal point. 
 
• Here are two examples of sentences that contain gerunds:
 
 
• As a food blogger, **eating **is an involved production for Shoshanna. 
 
• Fazal turned off his phone and shut the door so he could focus on **studying**.

P. One day while keeping the old books in a box

Q. But its beauty lies in its eternal movement.

questions.solution:
